name: S2-COMPRESSED-ACT row 6: the first bootable clip act — Emerald Hill Zone act 1, five sections of it, as far as the donor's own painted content reaches
note: WHY THIS RECTANGLE. (1) IT IS THE ACT'S FULL WIDTH, and the act is FIVE sections (10240 px) because that is the widest whole number of sections Emerald Hill has content for. The number that binds is the donor's own crop: zone.json extent.crop_tiles ends at tile 1372, i.e. x < 10976 px, and clip_manifest R9 refuses a src rect past it because outside the crop there is only the converter's zero padding. Six sections would need 12288. So 'EHZ is six sections wide' — true of its PADDED grid and written in this file before parcel 9 — is not true of its painted content: 10976 px of it is real and the last 1312 px of section 6 is padding. Five sections is the largest act whose every column the donor can paint, and painting every column is the whole point: the owner's complaint was a hard vertical edge where the painted world stopped. (2) Its height is 1024 and not 2048 because EHZ's whole crop is 128 tiles tall (zone.json extent.crop_tiles) and R9 refuses a rect past it — so the act's lower two section rows stay air, and a fall still has no bottom (see unpainted_remainder.unbounded_fall). (3) src == dst, so the paste SHIFT is (0,0): R12's 16-px block quantum is satisfied by construction, and a collision misalignment — which moves ground 8 px and which no screenshot shows — cannot hide behind a nonzero shift here. (4) dst (0,0) puts painted geometry in SECTION 0, which is the section whose block blob and local map own the map.toml head labels (OJZ_Sec0_Blocks / OJZ_Sec0_LocalMap); an all-air section 0 would content-dedup into an `equ` alias of some other section and the placement rows would name a label that is not a section head. (5) It is the opening of Emerald Hill act 1 and then nearly all of the rest of it — the most recognisable ground in Sonic 2 and therefore the clearest possible answer to 'is this our engine drawing Sonic 2'. (6) EHZ has ZERO cells on CRAM line 0 (verified in its zone.json counts, not assumed), so the palette defect parcel 2 measured in CPZ and WFZ cannot appear here. (7) The act stops 416 px short of where Sonic 2's own camera box for EHZ act 1 stops (camera_box_px x max 10656), so the very end of the level — where the signpost stands — is inside the donor's crop but not inside a whole fifth section. That is the cost of keeping the act's width a whole number of sections, and it is 416 px.

unpainted_remainder.why: NOTHING IS UNPAINTED ON THE X AXIS. 10240 is the act's own width (grid_w 5 x SECTION_SIZE 2048), so this names the end of the act rather than an edge inside it: the painted foreground runs to the last column the camera can reach, and EDGE_CLAMP stops the camera there. Parcel 6 painted 4096 px of a 6144 px act and parcel 7 measured the consequence — at x=4096 the art and BOTH collision planes stopped dead, top to bottom, because the tile cache carries the nametable and both planes in the same block, and the player walked off the painted world and fell the act's full height. Parcel 8 filled that act instead of shrinking it (the owner's call). Parcel 9 made the ACT'S OWN GRID something a clip can declare (the grid is generated into games/sonic4/data/generated/ojz/act1/act_grid.emp and the descriptor reads it), so the act grew from 3 sections to 5 and the clip grew with it. The declaration is KEPT rather than deleted because it is two-sided: clip_reachability.py refuses if the painted world ends anywhere but exactly x=10240, so if a future re-bake loses a section this says so instead of a report describing it later. THE Y AXIS IS A DIFFERENT STORY and is not fixed by this — see unbounded_fall below.

unbounded_fall.why: THE ACT STILL HAS NO BOTTOM. 1232 of the 1280 painted columns have air below their LAST landing surface, so a body that gets under the terrain has no floor anywhere in the 10240 px act and falls forever. (The other 48 are the two pits counted in floorless_columns instead: they have no landing surface at all to get under.) It is not a conversion defect: Sonic 2's terrain interiors are LRB-only ($2000 - solid left/right/bottom and NOTHING to a falling body), and Sonic 2 survives that with a LEVEL BOTTOM BOUNDARY that kills and restarts. EHZ act 1 declares its own at y=800 (s2_donor.level_size -> (0, 10656, 0, 800)). A clip act declares none, because this engine has no death of any kind yet, so there is nothing for a bottom boundary to do. The count went 512 -> 744 -> 1232 as the clip went two sections -> three -> five: more painted ground means more columns whose interior a body can get under, which is the honest arithmetic and not a regression. THE COUNT IS THE CHECK: add a floor, a death plane or a bottom boundary and it drops, and this gate says so.

floorless_columns.why: EMERALD HILL ACT 1'S OWN BOTTOMLESS PITS — TWO OF THEM NOW, at x 4672..4863 and x 9472..9663. These are not holes in the conversion — they are Sonic 2 level design, faithfully carried across: the art is fully drawn in every cell of every one of those columns (you SEE a pit), the collision cells are present, and they are the pits' LRB-only walls, so no column in either run carries a SOLID_TOP surface at any height on either plane. Sonic 2 ships them and survives them with the level bottom boundary at y=800 recorded in unbounded_fall above, which kills and restarts a player who falls in. THIS ENGINE HAS NO DEATH AT ALL, so here the same pits are endless falls. The first arrived with parcel 8's third section; the second arrived with parcel 9's fifth, and it was PREDICTED before it was measured — a wider act reaches more of Emerald Hill and Emerald Hill has more than one pit. Declared rather than refused because refusing would refuse faithful donor data for a hazard the donor game itself ships. THE RUNS ARE CHECKED EXACTLY, not just their count: a pit that MOVED with the count unchanged fails this gate (parcel 8's mutation B). Plane B is NOT declared and deliberately so: it is unreachable in this act (no crossover mark), its holes stay informational — there are four of them now, x runs (1344,1408), (4672,4864), (8192,8256), (9472,9664) — and the day something writes the player's layer byte they become a failure by name.
